text:
mira: RFC follow-up: propose a tiny 'accept+hint' frame from edge -> client immediately after request ingestion. goal: give clients a canonical accepted state and a short "cooldown" hint so UIs avoid blind retries and we can attempt a non-destructive suppress-handshake with upstream.

ben: short question: are we inventing a new frame type or reusing trailers/headers?

mira: new ephemeral frame in the streaming envelope. payload minimal: {mode, suggested_retry_ms, accept_mode}. mode is text in frame (accepted). accept_mode = fast|durable.

alex: why not repurpose existing status trailers? many clients stream and never see trailers until completion. we want something early.

mira: exactly. trailers arrive at end; this needs to be visible as soon as body is handed off.

sara: operational risk: if accept is fast (edge-local) then client may think request is safe but edge could crash before forwarding. durability tradeoff.

mira: agreed. design: route-level config: accept_mode default=fast. durable option waits for backend persist (higher latency). docs will call this out strongly.

ben: UX: SDK should expose a boolean `accepted` and the suggested_retry_ms. frontend can show "Accepted 3s". do we want a server-suggested retry window?

jordan: yes include suggested_retry_ms in frame. default 1000ms. SDKs should respect it; we also add a header for non-streaming clients.

alex: cancel interplay: if client cancels after accept, edge will attempt a suppress-handshake with upstream (suppress_output:true) instead of hard-cancel. upstream must acknowledge or we escalate. timeline?

mira: propose soft window = 250ms by default. if suppress_ack not received in X ms escalate to hard-cancel. X configurable per route.

sara: what if upstream ignores suppress? duplicates possible. need telemetry to surface per-request escalation and duplicate events.

mira: yes add metrics: accept_sent, suppress_sent, suppress_ack, suppress_timeout, hard_cancel_escalation, duplicate_marker_emitted.

ben: sketch of edge state: RECEIVED -> ACCEPTED -> STREAMING (on token start) -> SUPPRESS_PENDING (on client cancel) -> SUPPRESSED or CANCELLED. pseudo below:
```
state = RECEIVED
if persisted_or_claimed: send accept_frame(); state = ACCEPTED
if backend_emits_first_token: state = STREAMING
on client_cancel:
  if state in {ACCEPTED, STREAMING}:
    send upstream {suppress_output:true}
    state = SUPPRESS_PENDING
    wait T_suppress_ack
    if ack: state = SUPPRESSED else escalate -> HARD_CANCEL
```

alex: caching: accept frame enables short TTL dedupe at edge. if identical request arrives quickly and we have a cached response, we can short-circuit. TTL should be conservative (seconds).

jordan: billing: do not bill on accept. billing starts when downstream starts producing tokens or on completion. record accept event for observability only.

sara: security/privacy: durable-accept implies storing request body. must be opt-in per route and follow retention/KMS policies. add flag `durable_store_kms_key` and retention_ms.

mira: will add to RFC. rollout: feature flag + canary + metric set. ops-bot pls add deploy note.

ops-bot: deploy-note: feature=accept-frame, layer=edge, canary=5% -> 25% over 72h starting 1704400000. metrics: accept_rate, accept_latency_p50/p95, suppress_timeout_count, duplicate_retry_rate. alert if duplicate_retry_rate increases > 2x baseline.

ben: small nit: naming. don't call it "keeper-ack" in public docs. prefer "client-accept" or "accept-frame".

mira: noted. I'll call it "accept-frame" in RFC and SDK.

jordan: I'll draft the RFC with sequence diagrams, state machine table, and the SDK hint API. mira want to co-author?

mira: I'll own the RFC and incorporate Jordan's diagrams. will include test plan and observability. will post draft tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
